title: Agent governance lifecycle
summary: Govern a fleet of agents through five stages: inventory, identity, permissions, review and retirement. Every agent needs a sponsor, an identity with limited access, periodic review and a full shutdown path.
useIf: Agents are multiplying across teams and nobody can list them, say who owns them or revoke their access quickly.
avoidIf: You have one agent in a pilot: a simple owner, a ticket and a retirement date may be enough.

explain.md: **Inventory**: an unlisted agent is an ungoverned agent, so register every agent at build or deploy time. **Identity**: give each agent its own identity, not a shared service account. **Permissions**: grant least privilege and review it. **Review**: reconfirm purpose, access and behaviour on a schedule. **Retirement**: remove identity, credentials, memory, data and the registry entry. OWASP's agentic list names the failure modes this guards against, such as ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse and ASI10 Rogue Agents [[r22]].

Microsoft's control plane for this is **Agent 365**, generally available from 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment, licensed per user, with Microsoft E5 as the best-fit prerequisite. It observes, governs and secures agents through a registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Entra, Purview and Defender [[r17]] [[r24]]. In **Entra Agent ID**, at least one **sponsor** is required for each agent identity and blueprint: a business representative accountable for purpose and lifecycle. **Owners** are optional technical administrators. Sponsors can disable or soft-delete; owners can also re-enable, restore and hard-delete [[r18]]. Agents have no MFA, so access is governed with Conditional Access, which needs Microsoft 365 E7 or an Agent 365 licence with at least Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 [[r19]]. An agent identity is a service principal without credentials of its own; the blueprint holds credentials, and execution modes are S2S, OBO and Agentic-User, which needs the Frontier preview program [[r27]]. At the GA announcement, discovery of local and shadow agents through Defender and Intune was preview [[r24]].

explain.title: States of a governed agent
explain.alt: An agent moves from proposed to registered to active. Active agents are reviewed periodically, can be suspended on an incident or lapsed sponsor, and are eventually retired.
explain.src:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Proposed
  Proposed --> Registered: sponsor and identity assigned
  Registered --> Active: permissions approved
  Active --> InReview: periodic review
  InReview --> Active: access reconfirmed
  Active --> Suspended: incident or lapsed sponsor
  Suspended --> Active: restored
  Active --> Retired: sponsor retires it
  Retired --> [*]

Agents hold credentials or act on user data
An auditor or regulator asks who owns each agent
avoid: Governance by spreadsheet that nobody updates
Shared service accounts for many agents
Granting standing broad access because review is hard
flips: Agents run outside Microsoft 365: require registration at deploy time as a CI gate, and sync to a central inventory
A sponsor leaves: reassign before the agent is suspended
An incident occurs: suspend the identity first, then investigate

pitfalls.symptom: An agent keeps running after its builder left
pitfalls.cause: No sponsor succession; the sponsor was a person who moved on
pitfalls.fix: Require at least one sponsor, prefer a group or two people, and alert on lapsed sponsors [[r18]]
Give each agent its own identity and sponsor; avoid shared credentials

pitfalls.symptom: A retired agent still has access
pitfalls.cause: Only the app was deleted, not the identity, credentials, memory and registry entry
pitfalls.fix: Use a decommission checklist covering identity, credentials, memory, data and delisting

scenarios.title: Orphaned agents after a reorg
scenarios.situation: After a reorganisation, an access review finds eleven agents whose sponsors have left the company. Several still hold read access to HR data.
constraints: Agents are in Entra Agent ID
Business wants most to keep running
unknowns: Which agents still serve a purpose?
Who can be a successor sponsor?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Suspend the orphaned identities, assign successor sponsors per agent, then reinstate those that pass review
options.why: It stops access first, restores accountability and keeps useful agents.
options.tradeoff: A short outage for agents that matter.

options.name: Leave them running until someone complains
options.why: Agents with data access and no accountable sponsor are a risk with no owner.
options.tradeoff: Tolerable only for read-only, non-sensitive agents with a deadline.

options.name: Delete all eleven
options.tradeoff: Loses useful agents and evidence, and owners may be able to restore only soft-deleted ones.

flips.if: An agent is business critical and low-risk

flips.then: Use groups of eligible group types as sponsors.

scenarios.takeaway: Every agent needs a living sponsor.

scenarios.title: A mixed estate across clouds
scenarios.situation: Agents run in Microsoft 365, in a Kubernetes cluster and in another vendor's platform. Leadership wants one answer to 'how many agents do we have and who owns them'.
constraints: No single control plane covers all
unknowns: Which runtimes can integrate with Agent 365 or Entra Agent ID?
scenarios.question: How do you inventory?

options.name: A deploy-time registration gate for every runtime, synced to a central inventory that includes Agent 365 where applicable
options.why: A gate makes registration a condition of running, regardless of runtime, and the central view answers the question.
options.tradeoff: You build and maintain the gate and sync.

options.name: Rely on Agent 365 discovery alone
options.tradeoff: Shadow discovery was announced as preview at GA, and other runtimes may not be covered.

options.name: A shared spreadsheet
options.why: It is stale on day two and has no enforcement.

flips.if: Nearly all agents are in Microsoft 365
flips.then: Agent 365 and Entra become the primary inventory.

flips.if: Discovery reaches GA for your runtimes
flips.then: Use it to find unregistered agents and close the gap.

scenarios.takeaway: Make registration a condition of running.

scenarios.title: Retiring an agent
scenarios.situation: A team shuts down a customer-support agent and deletes its repository. Months later its credentials are found to be valid and its memory store still contains customer text.
constraints: Identity and credentials outlived the app
unknowns: Which stores hold memory and logs?
Which credentials belong to the blueprint?
scenarios.question: What should retirement have included?

options.name: A checklist: disable the identity, revoke credentials, delete memory and data, remove permissions and delist from the registry
options.why: Retirement is complete only when identity, credentials, memory, data and the registry entry are gone.
options.tradeoff: Effort at the end of a project, and evidence must be retained where law requires.

options.name: Delete the repository and the deployment
options.why: The identity, credentials and data survive.
options.tradeoff: Enough only for a throwaway prototype with none of those.

options.name: Disable the identity and leave it for later
options.tradeoff: Credentials and data persist, and later cleanup gets forgotten.

flips.if: A hold or audit requires evidence
flips.then: Retain logs under the legal rule and delete the rest.

flips.if: The agent may be restored soon
flips.then: Soft-delete or suspend with a dated review.

scenarios.takeaway: Retire the identity, the credentials, the memory and the registry entry.

quiz.q: Put the governance stages in order for a new agent, from first to last.
quiz.explain: An agent is registered, given its own identity and sponsor, granted least-privilege permissions, reviewed on a schedule and finally retired. This mirrors the five-stage lifecycle used in the Agent 365 and Entra guidance [[r17]] [[r18]].

quiz.q: In Entra Agent ID, which statement is correct?
options: At least one sponsor is required per agent identity; owners are optional
Owners are required and sponsors are optional
quiz.explain: Sponsors are required for agent identities and blueprints. Owners are optional technical administrators [[r18]].

quiz.q: Which belong in an agent decommission checklist?
options: Disable and delete the agent identity
Revoke credentials held by the blueprint
Delete memory and stored customer data
quiz.explain: Identity, credentials, memory and data must go with the registry entry. Deleting only the repository leaves live access behind.

flashcards.back: Inventory, identity, permissions, review, retirement. An unlisted agent is an ungoverned agent.

flashcards.front: Sponsor versus owner in Entra Agent ID?
flashcards.back: Sponsor: required business representative accountable for purpose and lifecycle. Owner: optional technical administrator who also manages credentials.
2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment, per user, with Microsoft E5 as best fit. Shadow-agent discovery was announced as preview then.
